RESULT: NOT ADOPTED. Candidate 0.442675 -> 0.443415 (+0.000741); paired per-fold diff mean +0.000741, 95% CI [-0.001316, +0.002797] INCLUDES 0, so the adoption gate fails. The gain is real but trivially small: 9 prediction flips out of 2699 rows, ALL from a wrong prediction, ZERO from a correct one, in every fold of both arms. WHY IT CANNOT PAY: a veto only changes the answer when the blend's argmax was inside the vetoed family, which almost never happens - the soft style rates already push those families down. ORACLE CONTROL: handing all 754 veto-fired rows to their true label gives BA 0.597166, but handing the SAME rows to truth with NO veto gives 0.597537 - the veto's own share of that ceiling is -0.000370, i.e. the large ceiling is just where the blend is wrong, not evidence for H9. METHOD CORRECTION FOUND HERE: the chance level (1-p)**n must count DISTINCT PROMPTS, not rows - 2699 rows are 150 prompt groups, so row-level confidence was overstated by orders of magnitude. Group-aware chance drops the two curly_dquote->ZAI rules (chance 1.04e-04 rows -> 1.48e-02 prompts) and 10 of 22 rules total, with the score UNCHANGED at 0.443415. The pooled prevalence p overstates Google's own em-dash rate, so an i.i.d. chance calculation cannot validate an absence rule when family base rates differ - and the family-specific rate is exactly what a zero-hit family cannot supply. Cross-fold recurrence filtering would remove the bad rule but is NOT usable: fold k's validation rows sit in fold j's training rows, so selecting rules by recurrence is the transductive class D026 bans (recorded as descriptive only).
